Occasion · marketing calendar
Choosing an occasion fills in the title, top line, caption, subject, letter and the message options for it — your name, photo, recipient and company facts stay. Edit anything afterwards; the {n} figure and this fact are reused in every message (update it when the London office is no longer new). "Custom occasion" keeps all text as it is.

No photo — the design adapts
  1. Type the recipient’s name above — the card updates instantly.
  2. Copy greeting image for email.
  3. In Outlook, Gmail or any mail app: New message → click in the body → Paste (Ctrl+V / ⌘V). The greeting appears as one picture.
  4. Paste the subject, add a line of text if you like, and send. Send one to yourself first to check.
  1. Add your name, designation, photo and message. Pick one of the three designs below.
  2. Download PNG (or Copy image) and Copy caption.
  3. LinkedIn → Start a post → Add media → choose the PNG → paste the caption → Post.
  1. Add your name, designation, photo and message. Pick one of the three designs below.
  2. Download PNG to your phone (or send it to yourself) and Copy caption.
  3. WhatsApp → Status → Add status → Photos → choose the PNG → paste the caption → Send.
Why an image: a single picture renders identically in every mail client (Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail, phones). HTML greetings with embedded images are often blocked or broken on the receiving side.
Sizes follow platform guidance: LinkedIn portrait 4:5 (1080 × 1350) and WhatsApp status 9:16 (1080 × 1920) with the top and bottom kept clear for the status bar and reply box.
Message options
Three suggested messages per platform. Edit any of them, regenerate the suggestion, or copy one as your caption. The selected option can also be placed in the artwork instead of the personal message.

Personalise in bulk — recipients or senders
Upload a CSV or Excel list (columns like Name, Designation, Company) or add rows by hand. Each row becomes its own email greeting and Story Letter — “Dear Rahul Sharma,” with “CTO · ABC Bank” beneath — and nothing else about them is invented.Upload a CSV or Excel list (columns like Sender name, Designation, Department, Photo, Message) or add rows by hand. Each row becomes its own set of creatives signed by that sender: the email and Story Letter carry a single signature, the LinkedIn post and WhatsApp status carry their name, designation and photo. “Photo” is the file name of a picture you upload below; “Message” replaces the short personal message if present.
